$comment: The enforcement matrix for city principles 15.1-15.9 (workbook section 23, stage P2-I; see docs/city/OWNER_CONTINUOUS_CONSTRUCTION_WORKBOOK.md). The matrix is DATA rather than prose so that scripts/principle-enforcement-validator.cjs can check every claim in it: a row may not say MACHINE_ENFORCED unless the guard it names EXISTS, is READ-ONLY, exits 0 when run, is reached by a test the required tiers execute, and reports a measured value at or below a target of 0. That rule exists because the cheapest lie a matrix of this kind can tell is to promote a ratchet into an enforcement, and workbook section 23 says plainly: do not fake semantic certainty. Every row whose strength is below its required strength must carry why_not_enforced, so the gap is recorded rather than hidden.

strength_semantics.MACHINE_ENFORCED: a guard fails on ANY violation; the resolved measured value must be at or below the target and the target must be 0
strength_semantics.MACHINE_RATCHET: a guard refuses a REGRESSION but the principle's target is not met, so the measured value is above the target and the row must say so
strength_semantics.EVIDENCE_REQUIRED: the principle cannot be fully automated without pretending to solve a semantic judgement, so the machine enforces that the EVIDENCE exists and an explicit structured decision record names the judgement
strength_semantics.NOT_GUARDED: nothing checks this, and the row must name the stage that owns the gap

principles.claim: foundation must not depend on building
principles.why_not_enforced: the guard refuses a RISE, and the measured count is 73 rather than 0. Recording this row as MACHINE ENFORCED would promote a regression floor into a claim the tree does not support.
principles.gap: the migration to 0 is stage P2-B, declared per plot in config/city-flatness.json

principles.claim: size is not itself a defect signal
principles.evidenceRequirement: every structural change records the MINIMUM STABLE SEMANTIC CLOSURE it migrated, and why that unit is semantic rather than a file count, in the construction ledger and in a closure record
principles.why_not_enforced: no enforcement rule in this repository keys its threshold on a file count, but nothing MACHINE-CHECKS that, and a check for 'did the author reason semantically' would be a judgement dressed up as a test.
principles.gap: the evidence requirement is enforced only as the EXISTENCE of a named decision record

principles.claim: minimum stable closure is the unit of migration
principles.requiredStrength: MACHINE CHECKED where decidable + explicit review record
principles.evidenceRequirement: each migration step states the closure it moved, what it deliberately did NOT move, and the measured before/after counts, so the step can be reviewed as a closure rather than as a diff
principles.why_not_enforced: the decidable half IS checked -- whether a closure is complete and well-formed is what scripts/capability-closure-validator.cjs decides, and tests/unit/city/provider-closure.test.ts pins the provider closure's completeness by name. Whether a GIVEN bundle of files is one purpose or seven remains a design judgement.
principles.gap: the judgement half is a review record, not a check

principles.claim: capability replacement lifecycle exists and carries one real proof
principles.why_not_enforced: no replacement-governance mechanism exists, so there is nothing to check and no state for a lifecycle to be in.
principles.gap: stage P2-G has not been started

principles.claim: least-sufficient repair: no PROHIBITED ADDED lateral load
principles.requiredStrength: MACHINE CHECK on prohibited added lateral load
principles.note: This is the row where the distinction matters. Section 23 asks for a check on ADDED lateral load, not on the absolute count, and that is exactly what the guard does: a rise in kernel -> feature edges, in kernel -> feature pairs or in mutual capability pairs fails. The absolute count still being 73 is principle 15.1's problem, not this row's claim.

principles.claim: every plot has exactly one valid flatness state
principles.note: Enforced as the STATE MACHINE: exactly one state per plot from the five, the per-state obligations, and a refusal to record FLAT on a plot that a measured defect implicates. That the seal is not ready is another row's fact -- config/city-flatness.json records 22 plots still mid-migration, and the seal gate says so rather than this one.

principles.claim: no cycles, no uncontrolled lateral bearing, no cross-domain private state access
principles.why_not_enforced: all guards refuse a REGRESSION and every part is still above 0: 38 mutual pairs, a largest component of 20 of 28 capabilities, and 5 private-state accesses over 3 (namespace, capability) pairs.
principles.gap: the migrations to 0 are stages P2-C and P2-D, declared per plot in config/city-flatness.json

principles.why_not_enforced: the ownership map has ONE named non-capability class -- composition_root -- and that is an explicit classification, but no ROAD class exists, and the one road candidate, electron/commander/**, is identified only in prose. Re-attributing it was measured and REFUTED (ledger CC-030): it has 132 incoming and 122 outgoing edges, so a road label would HIDE its edges rather than classify them.
principles.gap: stage P2-E has not been started; the extraction needs its five named proofs

principles.note: Core is defined by a stable classification -- a capability is Core if and only if its manifest declares kind: kernel -- and the city-phase starting surface (four capabilities, 115 owned files, plus a separately counted composition root of 2) is recorded in config/core-budget.json and pinned BY NAME, because a count of four would still read four if a kernel lost its kind and an unrelated capability gained one. The measured quantity is growth NOT covered by an Owner-approved exception, so this row stays at 0 when section 22's exception path is used and rises when growth is unapproved. What is proved today is the BAN: no exception has yet been recorded, so the exception path is exercised only on fixtures, and the budget says so rather than implying a governance mechanism has been used.
